The initial state is \(|3,0,0\rangle\) (3s). It decays via two dipole transitions to \(|1,0,0\rangle\) (1s). Dipole selection rules require \(\Delta l = \pm 1\), so the intermediate state must have \(l=1\). The only accessible intermediate state with lower energy is \(n=2\) (2p), since \(n=3\) states are degenerate in non-relativistic theory and transitions between them have zero rate.
